children.text: نمت صناعة الألعاب الصينية بشكل هائل في السنوات القليلة الماضية. الألعاب المجانية عبر الإنترنت، مثل Genshin Impact وWuthering Waves، لديها ملايين اللاعبين حول العالم، بينما تستعد أخرى مثل Etheria: Restart للإطلاق الكامل.
تطوير الألعاب الفردية يصبح مستداماً في الصين
كان المطورون الصينيون مترددين تاريخياً في العمل على الألعاب الفردية. تحديات إنتاج الألعاب الفردية المدفوعة هائلة، وشعبية الألعاب المجانية تجعل هذا النوع من الألعاب احتمالاً تجارياً أفضل.

يعطي تشو درساً موجزاً في التاريخ حول كيف أصبحت الألعاب المجانية المعيار لعقود عديدة: "إذا تذكرتم، كان عام 1995 عاماً فاصلاً شهد ولادة سلسلة أسطورة السيف والجنية. لسوء الحظ، حتى مع شعبية السلسلة، كانت القرصنة منتشرة جداً في ذلك الوقت لدرجة أن سوق الألعاب الفردية لم يستطع أن يزدهر حقاً."
النجاحات الأخيرة:
لعبة Black Myth: Wukong حققت نجاحاً مذهلاً، حيث باعت 10 مليون نسخة في أقل من أسبوع عند إطلاقها في أغسطس 2024، وحُكمت لاحقاً كلعبة العام في جوائز Steam 2024.
التحديات والفرص في سوق متقلب
الخبراء الذين تحدثنا معهم اتفقوا على أن مطوري الألعاب الصينيين يستفيدون من مزايا تنافسية فريدة ويكافحون مع بعض العيوب:
المزايا:
الشركات الصينية، بسبب خبرتها في صنع الألعاب المجانية عبر الإنترنت، هي رائدة عالمياً في التصميم التجاري والعمليات
تتفوق في إنشاء نماذج تحقيق الدخل وتوازن القيم الرقمية وتوجيه سلوك المستخدم
التحديات:
للأسف، تصميم الألعاب والجودة الإجمالية قد يقصران، خاصة في السرد وكتابة السيناريو
الصناعة لا تزال تعاني من خبرة محدودة في تصميم الألعاب ونظرة السوق غير الكافية وتبادل صناعي غير مناسب
الاستثمار الحكومي المحلي في تطوير الألعاب

السياسات الإقليمية تلعب دوراً كبيراً في دعم تطوير الألعاب في الصين. معظم الألعاب المقرر نشرها في البلاد تتطلب ترخيصاً من الإدارة الوطنية للصحافة والنشر (NPPA)، مع خطوات رئيسية تشمل مراجعة المحتوى والامتثال التقني.
الدعم الحكومي:
حكومة مقاطعة سيتشوان كانت داعمة جداً للعمل
حسب السياسات الإقليمية، قد تشمل المبادرات إعفاءات ضريبية للمشاريع الثقافية أو منح للتكنولوجيا والبحث والتطوير
الاتجاهات المستقبلية
لا يمكن إنكار أن الصين هي أكبر سوق ألعاب فيديو في العالم. بينما توجد تحديات مثل نقص الخبرة في صنع الألعاب الفردية والتردد في المخاطرة بإيرادات يوم الإطلاق، يبقى الخبراء متفائلين.
"الدخول المتزايد والطلب المتزايد على المحتوى عالي الجودة سيستمر في قيادة النمو"، كما يقول شين، مجادلاً بأن هناك مستقبلاً أكثر إشراقاً في المقدمة.

en.title: China's Gaming Industry: Market Size, Rules and Growth Opportunities
en.excerpt: China is the world's largest games market, home to Genshin Impact and Black Myth: Wukong. Here is how the industry works, what the licensing rules are, and where a Gulf business can take part.
en.seoDescription: China's gaming industry explained: market size, free-to-play strengths, NPPA licensing, and practical openings for Gulf publishers, retailers and investors.

children.text: Your customers in Riyadh, Kuwait or Dubai already play Chinese games, often without knowing it. China's gaming industry has grown into the largest in the world, and its studios now look abroad for players, partners and publishers. By the end of this guide you will know how the market developed, where Chinese developers are strong and weak, what the licensing rules mean for foreigners, and which openings suit a Gulf business.
How big is China's gaming industry?

China's gaming industry has grown very fast in recent years. Free-to-play online games such as Genshin Impact and Wuthering Waves have millions of players worldwide, and others such as Etheria: Restart have been preparing for full launch. China had 668 million players by the end of 2023 and in 2024 overtook the United States as the world's largest video game market. The wider numbers, including revenue forecasts to 2028, are set out in our guide to
China's entertainment and media industry

For a Gulf reader, the scale matters for one reason: Chinese studios have money, experience and a need to grow outside a crowded home market. The Middle East, with young, high-spending players, is one of the regions they target.
Why free-to-play dominated, and why that is changing
Piracy shaped the business model

Chinese developers were long hesitant to make single-player, pay-once games. The cost of producing a paid standalone title is high, and free-to-play games made a better commercial case. A developer named Zhou traces this to 1995, when the Legend of Sword and Fairy series launched. The series was popular, but piracy was so widespread that the market for paid standalone games could not survive. Studios moved to online games that earn from in-game purchases, which pirates cannot copy, and that model became the standard for decades.
Black Myth: Wukong proved paid games can sell

The picture changed in August 2024. Black Myth: Wukong sold 10 million copies in less than a week after release and was later named Game of the Year at the 2024 Steam Awards. Its success showed Chinese investors that a large, story-driven game made in China can earn at global scale, and more studios are now working on premium titles.
Where Chinese developers lead and where they fall short
Industry experts agree that Chinese developers have clear strengths and some known gaps. Knowing both helps you choose what to buy from them and what to bring yourself.
Strength
: after years of free-to-play games, Chinese companies lead the world in commercial design and live operations.
Strength
: they excel at monetisation models, balancing in-game economies and guiding player behaviour.
Weakness
: game design and overall quality can fall short, especially in narrative and script writing.
Weakness
: the industry still has limited experience in standalone game design, gaps in market insight and too little exchange with the wider industry.
That gap in market insight is where a Gulf partner adds value. Chinese studios rarely understand Arabic players, local payment habits or cultural sensitivities, and they know it.
Licensing and government support
The NPPA licence

Most games released in China need a licence from the National Press and Publication Administration (NPPA). The key steps are content review and technical compliance. Approvals are issued in batches, and waiting times vary. Foreign games need a separate import approval, and they are normally published through a licensed Chinese company. China also restricts foreign ownership of online publishing, so a foreign firm cannot simply set up a studio and publish directly to Chinese players.
Local incentives

Regional policy plays a large role. The Sichuan provincial government has been very supportive of game development, and depending on local rules, incentives can include tax exemptions for cultural projects or grants for technology and research and development. Other cities, including Shanghai, Shenzhen and Hangzhou, run their own programmes. Ask the local investment bureau for the current terms in writing before you decide where to set up.
Opportunities for Gulf businesses
Publishing and localisation for Arabic players

Chinese studios want regional publishers who can translate, localise, market and run customer service in Arabic. The strongest deals give you exclusive rights for the Middle East and North Africa for a set period, with a revenue share and clear targets. Check who owns the game's rights outside China before you negotiate; some titles are already licensed to a global publisher.

Budget for the real work of localisation. Arabic text runs right to left, so menus, fonts and chat need engineering work, not only translation. Voice-over, cultural review of characters and symbols, and age rating by the relevant regulator, such as Saudi Arabia's media authority, all take time. Plan 3 to 6 months from signed contract to regional launch for a mid-sized mobile game. Offer the payment methods Gulf players use: app store billing, local cards, mobile carrier billing and gift cards sold in shops.
Gaming hardware and accessories

Shenzhen and Dongguan make most of the world's gaming peripherals: headsets, keyboards, mice, controllers, gaming chairs, monitors and PC cases. Guangzhou's Panyu district supplies arcade machines and entertainment centre equipment. MOQs for branded peripherals often start at 500 to 1000 units per model, lower for stock designs. A
product sourcing service
can compare factories and check samples before you commit.

Production of peripherals usually takes 25 to 40 days after sample approval, and sea transit from Shenzhen to Jebel Ali or Dammam takes 18 to 30 days. Wireless controllers and headsets contain lithium batteries, so they must be declared and packed as dangerous goods. Ask for the certificates your market requires, such as radio approval for wireless devices, before production, not after the goods arrive.
Esports and events

Esports became medal events at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou, and Saudi Arabia now hosts major tournaments in Riyadh. Chinese teams, tournament organisers and broadcasting technology firms look for Gulf partners for venues, sponsorship and production. China's technology base behind this is covered in
investment opportunities in China's technology sector
How to start working with Chinese game companies
Choose your role: publisher, hardware importer, investor or event partner. Each needs different contacts and contracts.
Build a shortlist. Visit ChinaJoy in Shanghai, held each summer, or study studios active on global app stores and Steam.
Ask for proof of rights. For publishing, confirm who holds rights in your region; for hardware, ask for test reports and certificates for your market.
Register your brand in China before you share designs or names, because China grants trademarks to the first filer.
Start with a limited deal: one title, one region or one product line, with measurable targets over 6 to 12 months.
Put the contract under a neutral law and arbitration seat, such as Hong Kong or Singapore, and set payment and reporting terms clearly.
Protect your name first with
trademark registration in China
, including a Chinese-character version if you plan to sell there.
Common mistakes
Signing a publishing deal without confirming who holds the rights in the Middle East.
Assuming a foreign company can publish games directly to Chinese players without a licensed local partner.
Buying peripherals on price alone without checking certification for your market and warranty support.
Localising only the language and ignoring cultural review, which can get a game removed from regional app stores.
Relying on a studio's download figures without seeing revenue data for comparable regions.
What to do next

Experts remain optimistic about China's gaming industry. Challenges remain, including limited experience with standalone games and caution about launch-day revenue, but as an expert named Shen puts it, more entrants and growing demand for high-quality content will keep driving growth. This week, pick your role, list five Chinese studios or factories that fit it, and send each a short introduction with your market data. If you plan to meet them in person, HiGreenPanda can arrange
trade fair accompaniment
at ChinaJoy and factory visits in Shenzhen. File your trademark before the first meeting.

keyTakeaways: China's gaming industry is the world's largest, and its studios actively look for Middle East publishing and distribution partners.
Chinese developers lead in monetisation and live operations but often need help with narrative, localisation and regional market insight.
Most games need an NPPA licence, and foreign firms normally publish in China through a licensed local company.
Gaming peripherals from Shenzhen and Dongguan often start at MOQs of 500 to 1000 units per model; test samples first.
Confirm regional rights and register your trademark in China before signing any deal.

faqs.question: Is China the largest gaming market in the world?
faqs.answer: Yes. China overtook the United States in 2024 to become the world's largest video game market, with 668 million players by the end of 2023. Free-to-play online games make up most of its revenue.

faqs.question: Why are most Chinese games free-to-play?
faqs.answer: Piracy in the 1990s made paid standalone games hard to sell, so studios moved to online games that earn from in-game purchases. That model became the standard, and Chinese companies now lead the world in monetisation and live operations.

faqs.question: How successful was Black Myth: Wukong?
faqs.answer: Black Myth: Wukong sold 10 million copies in less than a week after its release in August 2024. It was later named Game of the Year at the 2024 Steam Awards, and it encouraged more Chinese studios to invest in premium games.

faqs.question: Do games need a licence to be released in China?
faqs.answer: Most do. The National Press and Publication Administration reviews content and technical compliance before issuing a licence. Foreign games need import approval and are normally published through a licensed Chinese company.

faqs.question: How can a Gulf company work with Chinese game studios?
faqs.answer: Common routes are regional publishing and Arabic localisation, importing gaming hardware, investing in studios, and partnering on esports events. Start with a limited deal, confirm who holds the rights in your region, and register your trademark in China first.

en.title: China's Construction Industry: Trends and Sourcing Opportunities
en.excerpt: China's construction industry is growing at about 3.9% a year to 2028, driven by infrastructure, urbanisation and green building. Here is what that means for a Gulf buyer sourcing materials and machinery.
en.seoDescription: China's construction industry explained for Gulf buyers: growth to 2028, green and digital trends, and how to source building materials and machinery safely.

children.text: You are pricing a project in Riyadh, Dubai or Aden, and the Chinese quote for tiles, steel or an excavator is well below the local one. Before you commit, you need to know how China's construction industry works, where it is heading, and where buyers lose money. By the end of this guide you will know which trends matter to you, which products are worth sourcing, and the steps to order without surprises.
How big is China's construction industry and where is it heading?

Construction has long been a cornerstone of China's economic development. It has driven infrastructure growth and urbanisation on a scale no other country has matched: motorways, high-speed rail, ports, airports and entire new city districts. That scale built a supply chain for cement, steel, glass, ceramics, cables, pumps and heavy machinery that now serves buyers worldwide.
Growth is expected to stay steady. Reports indicate an average annual growth rate of
3.9% between 2025 and 2028

, supported by government investment in infrastructure and a focus on sustainable development. That is slower than the boom years, and the difference matters to you. The domestic housing market has cooled since 2021, so many factories built for that boom now have spare capacity and actively look for export orders. For a buyer, this usually means shorter queues and more room to negotiate on price and payment terms.
Urbanisation and infrastructure upgrades

Urbanisation remains a fundamental driver of construction activity. Cities such as Beijing and Shanghai are going through extensive infrastructure upgrades: metro extensions, drainage, district heating and the retrofitting of older buildings. China now prioritises infrastructure projects that deliver clear economic benefits, rather than building for the sake of volume. Suppliers who serve these projects are used to tender documents, test reports and third-party inspection, which makes them easier to work with on a Gulf project that has a consultant and a specification.
Trends that change what you can buy
Green building initiatives

Sustainability is reshaping the Chinese construction landscape. Government policy pushes green buildings and energy-efficient infrastructure, so factories now offer insulated panels, low-emissivity glass, solar-ready roofing, LED lighting and water-saving sanitary ware as standard lines. This lines up with Gulf requirements such as Estidama in Abu Dhabi, the Dubai Green Building Regulations and the energy-efficiency rules that Saudi Arabia applies to air conditioners and lighting. Ask for the test report behind every energy claim, and read
how to choose environmentally friendly suppliers
before you shortlist.
Digital transformation

Digital tools are spreading fast through the sector. Artificial intelligence and predictive analytics help Chinese contractors plan work, control costs and forecast demand, and many producers now run automated lines for steel structures, precast concrete and windows. The practical gain for you is consistency: a factory that cuts steel by CNC machine from your drawings makes fewer errors than one that cuts by hand. The wider shift is covered in
how China leads the smart manufacturing revolution
What Gulf buyers source from China for construction

Most of what you need for a building project can be sourced from China. The question is whether the saving survives freight, duty and compliance. These categories usually do, provided the order is large enough to fill containers.
Ceramic and porcelain tiles
: mostly from Foshan in Guangdong. Heavy, so a 20ft container fills by weight long before it fills by volume.
Sanitary ware and taps
: Chaozhou and Kaiping for ceramics, Wenzhou and Nan'an for brass fittings.
Aluminium profiles, windows and curtain wall
: Foshan and Guangzhou. Check alloy grade and coating thickness in writing.
Steel structures and prefabricated buildings
: warehouses, site offices and labour camps, cut and drilled to drawing and shipped flat.
Cables, switches and LED lighting
: Zhejiang and Guangdong. These are regulated products in most Gulf states.
Heavy machinery
: excavators, loaders, cranes and concrete pumps from large manufacturers, new or used, often shipped RoRo or on flat racks.
Match each product to a region first, then to a factory. A trading company in Shanghai can sell you tiles, but the factory in Foshan will quote lower and answer technical questions faster.
Challenges you will meet
Regulations on both sides

Compliance with China's complex regulatory environment remains a challenge for foreign firms that want to build or invest inside China, where licences and local partners are required. For an importer the bigger issue sits at home. Saudi Arabia requires a certificate of conformity through SABER for most regulated building and electrical products. The UAE applies conformity schemes for electrical goods and some construction products. Before you order, confirm the standard, the certificate and who pays for testing, and check the current list with your customs broker or the national standards body.
Labour shortage and rising wages

China's labour market faces increasing constraints. Fewer young workers join building sites and factories, and wages have risen. Companies respond with automation and AI-powered tools. For you, this means Chinese prices rise gradually rather than fall, and factories with automated lines hold quality better than those that rely on casual labour. The cost effect is explained in
the impact of China's changing workforce on wages
How to source construction materials from China step by step
Freeze the specification. Take the consultant's approved drawings and data sheets and turn them into a one-page spec per item: size, grade, finish, standard and tolerance.
Confirm the import rules at home. Ask your broker which items need a conformity certificate, what the duty rate is (5% is common in the GCC, with exceptions) and how long clearance takes.
Shortlist three to five factories in the right region. Ask each for a business licence, export history to the Gulf and test reports from a recognised laboratory.
Order samples and test them against the spec. For tiles check size, flatness and water absorption; for steel ask for mill certificates matched to heat numbers.
Negotiate price, lead time and payment. A 30% deposit and 70% against a copy of the bill of lading is common. Production usually takes 15 to 45 days depending on product and season.
Book an independent inspection before the balance is paid. Count cartons, open a sample, and compare against the approved sample.
Plan freight by weight, not just volume. Sea transit from southern China to Jebel Ali or Dammam usually takes 18 to 30 days port to port.
A
pre-shipment quality inspection
typically costs a few hundred USD per visit. On a container of tiles or cables worth tens of thousands, it costs far less than a rejected delivery on site.
Common mistakes when buying building materials from China
Buying from photographs and price alone, without a sample tested against the project specification.
Accepting a factory's own test report when the consultant or authority requires an accredited third-party laboratory.
Forgetting that tiles, steel and stone max out container weight. Road limits at both ends can cap a 20ft container well below its rated payload.
Mixing tile production batches. Shades vary between batches, so require one batch per area and the batch number on every carton.
Ignoring the conformity certificate until the goods arrive, then paying demurrage while testing is done.
Paying 100% up front to a supplier you have never visited or had inspected.
Opportunities beyond importing

Chinese contractors and machinery makers are active across the Gulf, and many look for local partners, distributors and subcontractors. If you already supply sites at home, a distribution agreement with a Chinese brand of pumps, lifts or machinery can be worth more than one-off imports. If you want to go further and hold stock, run a buying office or invoice from China, a Chinese company becomes useful. Weigh this against
contract manufacturing in China
, which lets you put your own brand on products without owning a factory.
What to do next

This week, pick the one item on your project with the biggest price gap, such as tiles, windows or cabling. Write its one-page specification, call your customs broker to confirm the certificate and duty, and request quotes and samples from three factories in the right region. HiGreenPanda's team in Shenzhen and Shanghai can handle the
factory search and sample checks
on the ground if you cannot travel. Once samples pass, fix payment terms and book the inspection date before production starts, not after.

keyTakeaways: China's construction industry is expected to grow about 3.9% a year from 2025 to 2028, and spare factory capacity gives buyers room to negotiate.
Source each product from its home region, such as tiles from Foshan and brass fittings from Wenzhou, and buy from factories rather than traders where you can.
Confirm the conformity certificate and duty rate at home before ordering, because clearance delays on site cost more than the saving.
Test samples against the consultant's specification and book an independent inspection before paying the balance.
Plan heavy materials by container weight, not volume, and allow 18 to 30 days sea transit to Gulf ports.

faqs.question: How fast is China's construction industry growing?
faqs.answer: Reports indicate average annual growth of about 3.9% between 2025 and 2028. Growth is driven by government infrastructure spending, urbanisation and sustainable building. It is slower than the boom years, which leaves many material factories keen for export orders.

faqs.question: Which building materials are worth importing from China to the Gulf?
faqs.answer: Tiles, sanitary ware, aluminium windows, steel structures, cables, LED lighting and heavy machinery usually save money once freight and duty are included. The saving depends on filling containers and passing conformity testing at home, so price the full landed cost before you order.

faqs.question: Do Chinese building materials need certificates in Saudi Arabia or the UAE?
faqs.answer: Many do. Saudi Arabia requires a certificate of conformity through SABER for most regulated products, and the UAE applies conformity schemes to electrical goods and some construction products. Confirm the current rules with your customs broker or the national standards body before production starts.

faqs.question: How long does it take to ship construction materials from China to the Gulf?
faqs.answer: Production usually takes 15 to 45 days depending on the product and season. Sea transit from southern China to Jebel Ali or Dammam is typically 18 to 30 days port to port, plus clearance time at destination.

faqs.question: How do I avoid quality problems with Chinese tiles or steel?
faqs.answer: Approve a physical sample against your specification, require one production batch per area for tiles and mill certificates for steel, and book an independent inspection before paying the balance. Never pay the full amount up front to an unverified supplier.

children.text: وفقاً لتوقعات صناعة الترفيه والإعلام العالمية من PwC للفترة 2024 إلى 2028 ملخص الصين، ستصل إجمالي إيرادات صناعة الترفيه والإعلام الصينية إلى حوالي 576.2 مليار دولار أمريكي بحلول عام 2028. معدل النمو السنوي المركب (CAGR) البالغ 5.5% سيكون أعلى من المتوسط العالمي البالغ 3.9% خلال السنوات الخمس القادمة.
الإعلان عبر الإنترنت

السوق الصيني استمر في الحفاظ على نمو مستقر في عام 2024. مع توضيح السياسات واللوائح المحلية، نمو سوق الإعلان عبر الإنترنت الصيني سيستقر تدريجياً في السنوات القادمة. يُقدر أنه بحلول عام 2028، سيصل حجم سوق الإعلان عبر الإنترنت الصيني إلى حوالي 215.8 مليار دولار أمريكي بمعدل نمو سنوي مركب 10.8%.
العوامل المساهمة في النمو:
التطور السريع لتقنيات الإنترنت ونضج سلسلة القيمة
أشكال إعلان الفيديو القصير أصبحت أكثر تنوعاً
حوسبة البيانات لمنصات وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي للفيديو القصير أدت إلى وضع إعلانات أكثر دقة

مع انتشار نمط الحياة الرقمي، ستصل نفاذية الشبكة المحمولة في الصين إلى أكثر من 90%، مما سيكون له تأثير إيجابي على نمو الإعلان عبر الإنترنت الصيني. إعلان الفيديو عبر الإنترنت هو أسرع المكونات نمواً في الإعلان عبر الإنترنت محلياً، يُقدر أنه بحلول عام 2028، سيشكل 27% من إجمالي الإيرادات، بمعدل نمو سنوي مركب سيصل إلى 12.9% خلال السنوات الخمس القادمة.
فيديو التدفق المباشر (OTT)
مع تطور التقنيات مثل الذكاء الاصطناعي و5G، سوق فيديو OTT الصيني يتطور بثبات. من 2023 إلى 2028، يُتوقع أن يصل معدل النمو السنوي المركب إلى 4.7%.
أصبحت إدارة العضوية عبر الواجهات اتجاهاً رئيسياً في تطوير صناعة خدمة الشاشة الكبيرة OTT، مع تكامل إنترنت الأشياء-OTT الشاشة الكبيرة يوسع بشكل كبير حالات الاستخدام ويوفر للمستخدمين تغذية محتوى دقيقة.
عدد اشتراكات OTT متوقع أن يزيد بحوالي 55 مليون بحلول عام 2028، ارتفاعاً من 423 مليون في عام 2023 إلى 478 مليون.
ألعاب الفيديو والرياضات الإلكترونية

الصين هي أكبر سوق ألعاب فيديو ورياضات إلكترونية في العالم. بنهاية عام 2023، وصل إجمالي عدد لاعبي ألعاب الفيديو في الصين إلى 668 مليون. من المتوقع أن تنمو إجمالي الإيرادات بمعدل نمو سنوي مركب 13.3% من عام 2023 لتصل إلى 122.8 مليار دولار أمريكي بحلول عام 2028.
الإنجازات البارزة:
في عام 2024، استبدلت الصين الولايات المتحدة لتصبح أكبر سوق ألعاب فيديو في العالم
بسبب نموها السريع، السوق الصيني مقرر أن يحقق إيرادات أكثر بحوالي 47% من الولايات المتحدة بحلول عام 2028
ظهور ثمانية أحداث ميدالية رياضات إلكترونية في دورة الألعاب الآسيوية التاسعة عشرة هانغتشو في سبتمبر 2023
مع دعم سياسات الصناعة الثقافية وتحسينات في قدرة البحث والتطوير المستقل في القطاع، تعزز قدرة منتجات الألعاب الصينية التنافسية في الأسواق الخارجية بشكل ملحوظ، مع إمكانات قوية للتوسع المستقبلي.
يجدر بالذكر أن هذا العام، أول لعبة AAA محلية Black Myth: Wukong طورتها Game Science حصدت استحساناً في الصين وخارجها عند إطلاقها.
السينما

مع تعافي السوق الاستهلاكي المحلي بثبات، أظهرت السينما اتجاه تعافٍ يعمل كمؤشر ملحوظ للاستهلاك غير المتصل بالإنترنت. إيرادات شباك التذاكر الصيني انتعشت بنسبة 83% إلى 7.81 مليار دولار أمريكي في عام 2023، تشكل 24.14% من إيرادات شباك التذاكر العالمي.
إنجازات الربع الأول 2024:
استمر السوق السينمائي المحلي في التعافي بثبات
وصلت إيرادات شباك التذاكر المحلي إلى 14.36 مليار يوان صيني، بنمو سنوي 3.14%
عدد رواد السينما كان 364 مليون بنمو سنوي 8.15%

يُقدر أن تنمو إيرادات السينما الصينية بمعدل نمو سنوي مركب 7.15% من 2023 إلى 2028. تأثير شباك التذاكر الصيني على التصنيفات العالمية لشباك التذاكر ازداد، والأفلام المحلية لا تزال تهيمن على إيرادات شباك التذاكر الصيني.

خلال عام 2023، أُضيفت 1,801 شاشة جديدة، ومن المتوقع أن يستمر هذا النمو خلال فترة التوقعات. قدرة إنتاج الأفلام الصينية تستمر أيضاً في التحسن، بينما عرض الأفلام ينمو بثبات، مع توسع تدريجي للتأثير الدولي.

en.title: China's Entertainment and Media Industry: Growth and Opportunities
en.excerpt: PwC expects China's entertainment and media industry to reach about USD 576.2 billion by 2028. Here is where the growth is, what the rules allow foreigners to do, and where a Gulf business fits in.
en.seoDescription: China's entertainment and media industry to 2028: advertising, streaming, games and cinema figures, the rules for foreigners, and openings for Gulf firms.

children.text: You hear that China is now the biggest market for games, one of the largest for cinema, and the testing ground for short-video selling. The question for a Gulf business is simpler: where in China's entertainment and media industry can you actually buy, sell or partner, and what stops foreigners at the door? By the end of this guide you will know the size of each segment, the rules that shape entry, and the practical routes open to you.
How big is China's entertainment and media market?
According to PwC's Global Entertainment and Media Outlook 2024-2028, China Summary, total revenue in China's entertainment and media industry will reach about
USD 576.2 billion by 2028
. The compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of
is higher than the global average of 3.9% over the same five years.

The growth is uneven. Online advertising and video games grow fastest, streaming grows steadily, and cinema is still recovering. Each segment offers a different entry point, so read them separately rather than as one market.
Online advertising and short video

China's online advertising market kept growing steadily in 2024. As local policies and regulations become clearer, growth is expected to settle at a stable pace. PwC estimates the market will reach about
USD 215.8 billion by 2028
, with a CAGR of 10.8%.
Three factors drive this growth:
Rapid development of internet technology and a mature value chain from content creators to agencies and platforms.
More varied short-video advertising formats, from sponsored clips to live-stream selling.
Data computing on short-video social platforms, which places ads more precisely.

As digital lifestyles spread, mobile internet penetration in China will pass 90%, which supports further advertising growth. Online video advertising is the fastest-growing part of the market. It is expected to reach 27% of total online advertising revenue by 2028, with a CAGR of 12.9% over five years.
What this means for you

If you want to sell Gulf products such as dates, perfume, oud or tourism packages to Chinese consumers, you will reach them through Douyin, Xiaohongshu and WeChat, not through Western platforms. Foreign brands usually start through cross-border e-commerce stores or a Chinese company that can sign contracts with local agencies and influencers. The live-selling methods perfected in China also work at home, since TikTok and Douyin share the same owner and many of the same formats.
Streaming and over-the-top (OTT) video

With AI and 5G, China's OTT video market is developing steadily, with an expected CAGR of 4.7% from 2023 to 2028. Membership management through TV interfaces has become a major trend on large screens, and the integration of IoT devices with OTT platforms has widened use cases and made content feeds more precise.

OTT subscriptions are expected to rise by about 55 million by 2028, from 423 million in 2023 to 478 million. For Arab producers, Chinese platforms rarely buy Arabic-language content, but Chinese dramas and animation are increasingly licensed, dubbed or subtitled for Middle East audiences. That licensing flows from China outwards, and Gulf distributors can take part in it.
Video games and esports
China is the world's largest video game and esports market. By the end of 2023 it had 668 million players. PwC expects total revenue to grow at a CAGR of 13.3% and reach
USD 122.8 billion by 2028
In 2024 China overtook the United States to become the world's largest video game market.
By 2028 China's market is expected to earn about 47% more revenue than the United States.
Esports featured as eight medal events at the 19th Asian Games in Hangzhou in September 2023.

Cultural industry policy and stronger in-house research and development have made Chinese games far more competitive abroad. In August 2024, Black Myth: Wukong, the first domestic AAA game, developed by Game Science, was praised in China and internationally. The Gulf is already part of this story: Saudi Arabia hosts large esports events in Riyadh, and Chinese studios and teams take part. The full picture is in our guide to
China's gaming industry and its growth opportunities
Cinema and live entertainment

As domestic consumption recovered, cinema became a visible indicator of offline spending. China's box office recovered by 83% to USD 7.81 billion in 2023, which was 24.14% of global box office revenue. In the first quarter of 2024:
The domestic cinema market continued its steady recovery.
Box office revenue reached CNY 14.36 billion, up 3.14% year on year.
Cinema attendance reached 364 million, up 8.15% year on year.

Cinema revenue is expected to grow at a CAGR of 7.15% from 2023 to 2028. China's weight in global box office rankings has increased, and domestic films still dominate local takings. In 2023, 1801 new screens were added, and more are expected. Production capacity keeps improving, exhibition grows steadily, and the industry's international influence is widening.
The equipment behind the screens

For many Gulf buyers the most direct opportunity is equipment. Shenzhen is the centre for LED display panels, and Guangzhou's Panyu and Huadu districts supply stage lighting, sound systems, arcade machines and amusement rides. New cinemas, malls and entertainment venues across Saudi Arabia and the UAE buy these in volume. Order samples, check brightness, pixel pitch and heat tolerance, and have units inspected before shipment through a
product sourcing service
or your own team.
How to enter China's entertainment and media market
What rules limit foreign involvement?

China keeps tight control over content. Its foreign investment negative list prohibits or restricts foreign ownership in news, broadcasting, publishing and much of film production. Games need a licence from the National Press and Publication Administration before release. Foreign films enter under an annual quota for revenue-sharing titles, commonly cited at 34. In practice, foreigners take part through licensing, co-production, advertising services, technology supply and trade in equipment, not through owning media outlets.

The open doors are wider than they look. Equipment, software and advertising services face few ownership limits, and Chinese studios actively look for partners who can take their games, dramas and animation into Arabic-speaking markets. Localisation, dubbing, regional publishing and event organisation are all services Chinese firms buy rather than build.
Steps to take
Choose your route: selling to Chinese consumers, licensing Chinese content out, supplying technology, or importing equipment.
Check the rules for that route. Content and platforms are regulated; equipment trade and advertising services are far more open.
Decide whether you need a Chinese company. Contracts with Chinese agencies, influencers and platforms are much easier with a local entity and a Chinese bank account.
Register your trademark in China before you promote anything, since China grants marks to whoever files first.
Test with a small campaign or a sample order, measure the result in numbers, then scale.

Allow realistic time. A Chinese company usually takes 4 to 8 weeks to set up and open a bank account, a trademark filing takes around 12 months to register, and a first equipment order takes 20 to 40 days to produce plus sea freight. Budget for the test phase as a cost of learning, not as a sales channel. The wider technology context is set out in
investment opportunities in China's technology sector
Common mistakes
Treating China as one market. Advertising, streaming, games and cinema have different rules and buyers.
Planning to promote in China with Instagram, YouTube or Google, which are not accessible there.
Signing influencer or agency deals without a Chinese contract party, leaving you no practical recourse.
Promoting a brand before registering the trademark in China.
Buying LED screens or lighting on price alone without testing brightness, heat tolerance and spare-parts supply.
What to do next

This week, pick one route and write down what success looks like in numbers: units sold, screens installed or content licensed. If you want to sell to Chinese consumers, list the three platforms you will use and ask two agencies for a quote. If you are buying equipment, request specifications and samples from three factories in Shenzhen or Guangzhou. HiGreenPanda helps Gulf firms plan
e-commerce and platform launches in China
from its offices in Shenzhen and Shanghai. Whatever the route, file your trademark before you spend on promotion.

keyTakeaways: PwC expects China's entertainment and media industry to reach about USD 576.2 billion by 2028, growing 5.5% a year against 3.9% globally.
To sell Gulf products to Chinese consumers, plan for Douyin, Xiaohongshu and WeChat and a Chinese contract party.
Foreign ownership of Chinese media content is restricted, so enter through licensing, advertising, technology or equipment trade.
LED screens, stage lighting and arcade machines from Shenzhen and Guangzhou serve the Gulf's new cinemas and venues; test samples first.
Register your trademark in China before any promotion, because China grants marks to the first filer.

faqs.question: How big is China's entertainment and media industry?
faqs.answer: PwC's outlook puts total revenue at about USD 576.2 billion by 2028. That is a CAGR of 5.5%, above the global average of 3.9%. Online advertising and video games are the fastest-growing segments.

faqs.question: Can foreigners invest in Chinese media companies?
faqs.answer: Foreign ownership in news, broadcasting, publishing and most film production is prohibited or restricted under China's negative list. Foreign firms usually take part through licensing, co-production, advertising services, technology supply or equipment trade instead.

faqs.question: Is China the largest video game market in the world?
faqs.answer: Yes. China overtook the United States in 2024 and had 668 million players by the end of 2023. Revenue is expected to reach USD 122.8 billion by 2028, about 47% more than the United States.

faqs.question: How do I advertise a Gulf product to Chinese consumers?
faqs.answer: Use Chinese platforms such as Douyin, Xiaohongshu and WeChat, usually through a local agency and influencers. A Chinese company or a cross-border e-commerce store makes contracts and payments easier. Register your trademark in China before you start.

faqs.question: How is China's cinema market doing?
faqs.answer: The box office recovered by 83% to USD 7.81 billion in 2023, 24.14% of the global total. In the first quarter of 2024 revenue reached CNY 14.36 billion, and cinema revenue is expected to grow 7.15% a year to 2028.

ar.title: أسئلة وأجوبة حول صناعة التعدين في الصين
ar.excerpt: ج: الفحم (حصة كبيرة من الطاقة)، الحديد والصلب (إنتاج ضخم مع اعتماد على واردات الخام)، النحاس والألمنيوم (طلب مدفوع بالبنية التحتية والكهرباء)، العناصر الأرضية النادرة (ريادة عالمية في التعدين والمعالجة)، مع نمو الليثيوم والنيكل والكوبالت للبطاريات.
ar.seoDescription: ج: الفحم (حصة كبيرة من الطاقة)، الحديد والصلب (إنتاج ضخم مع اعتماد على واردات الخام)، النحاس والألمنيوم (طلب مدفوع بالبنية التحتية والكهرباء)، العناصر…

children.text: س: ما أبرز مكوّنات قطاع التعدين في الصين؟

ج: الفحم (حصة كبيرة من الطاقة)، الحديد والصلب (إنتاج ضخم مع اعتماد على واردات الخام)، النحاس والألمنيوم (طلب مدفوع بالبنية التحتية والكهرباء)، العناصر الأرضية النادرة (ريادة عالمية في التعدين والمعالجة)، مع نمو الليثيوم والنيكل والكوبالت للبطاريات.
س: ما التحديات البيئية الرئيسية؟
ج: معالجة المخلفات والسوائل الحمضية والغبار، وخفض كثافة الانبعاثات عبر الطاقة الأنظف وكفاءة الاستهلاك.
س: كيف تُعالج تحديات السلامة والامتثال؟
ج: تفتيش دوري وإغلاق المناجم عالية المخاطر، ورفع معايير السلامة في المناجم العميقة، وتحسين الإفصاح والحوكمة.
س: ما أثر تقلبات الأسواق؟
ج: حساسية عالية لأسعار السلع؛ تستخدم سياسات مخزون إستراتيجي والتحوط بالعقود الآجلة لتخفيف المخاطر، خاصة لاعتماد خام الحديد والنحاس.
س: أين يبرز الابتكار التقني؟
ج: مناجم ذكية مؤتمتة، إنترنت الأشياء، مركبات ذاتية، وتوأم رقمي لصيانة تنبؤية وتحسين الجداول.
س: ما الاتجاهات الاستراتيجية؟
ج: دمج الكيانات الصغيرة، تعزيز القيمة المضافة محليًا (خصوصًا في REEs والبطاريات)، واستثمارات خارجية لتأمين الإمدادات.
س: كيف يؤثر التحول الطاقي؟
ج: ارتفاع الطلب على النحاس والليثيوم والنيكل بفعل المركبات الكهربائية والطاقة المتجددة، مع تراجع تدريجي لدور الفحم.
س: ما الفرص للشركاء الدوليين؟
ج: معدات منخفضة الانبعاثات، تقنيات معالجة نظيفة، حلول السلامة، شراكات إعادة التدوير، وخدمات التحوط.
س: ما أطر الحوكمة ذات الصلة؟
ج: لوائح بيئية أشد، معايير إفصاح ESG، ودعم R&D للتعدين النظيف وإعادة التدوير الحضري.
س: ما وضع "التعدين الحضري" وإعادة التدوير؟
ج: تنمو مبادرات استخراج المعادن من المخلفات الإلكترونية وبقايا الصناعات، مع دعم حكومي لتوسيع القدرات وإدراجها في أهداف خفض الانبعاثات.
س: كيف تُدار العلاقات مع المجتمعات المحلية حول المناجم؟
ج: عبر آليات تشاور مبكر، وتعويضات عادلة، وبرامج تدريب وتشغيل بديلة، ومراقبة تأثيرات بيئية دورية شفافة للجمهور.
س: ما مؤشرات الأداء الرئيسة للقطاع؟
ج: معدل الحوادث لكل 1,000 عامل، كثافة الانبعاثات (طن CO2/طن خام)، نسبة النفايات المعالَجة، ومعامل الاسترداد المعدني في المعالجة.
س: إلى أين يتجه القطاع خلال 3–5 سنوات؟
ج: رقمنة أعمق للمناجم، مشاريع منخفضة الكربون، توسع في إعادة التدوير، وتدويل لسلاسل بطاريات المركبات الكهربائية.

en.title: China's Mining Industry: Questions and Answers for Traders
en.excerpt: What does China's mining industry produce, how is it regulated, and how do its price swings and export rules affect you as a buyer of steel, copper, batteries or solar equipment? Clear answers and practical steps.
en.seoDescription: China's mining industry explained: main minerals, safety and environmental rules, price risks, export controls, recycling and what they mean for importers.

children.text: If you buy steel, aluminium profiles, copper cable, batteries or solar equipment from China, your prices and delivery times depend on what happens in China's mining industry. A mine closure, a new export rule or a swing in iron ore prices can change a quotation within days. This guide answers the most common questions about the sector and, for each, explains what it means for you as an importer or investor. By the end you will know which materials to watch, which risks to plan for and what to check with suppliers.
What are the main parts of China's mining sector?
China mines and processes almost every major mineral, but five groups matter most for trade.
Coal

Coal still supplies more than half of China's primary energy. Its share is falling slowly as solar, wind and hydropower grow, but it remains the backbone of power supply and of steel production. When coal supply tightens, electricity rationing can slow factories, which is one reason delivery dates sometimes slip. Coal-fired power also matters for aluminium, because smelting uses large amounts of electricity; China caps its total aluminium smelting capacity at around 45 million tonnes a year, which limits how fast supply can respond to demand.
Iron ore and steel

China produces more than half of the world's crude steel but imports most of the iron ore it needs, mainly from Australia and Brazil. That dependence makes Chinese steel prices sensitive to seaborne ore prices. For construction and fabrication buyers, it is the single biggest driver of steel quotations. Our article on
China's construction industry
explains how domestic building demand adds to this.
Copper and aluminium

Demand for both is driven by infrastructure and electricity networks. China is the largest producer of aluminium and the largest consumer of copper, and it relies heavily on imported copper concentrate. Cables, transformers, air-conditioning parts and aluminium profiles all follow these metal prices.
Rare earth elements

China leads the world in rare earth mining and, by a wider margin, in processing. Rare earths go into magnets for electric motors, wind turbines and electronics. Since 2023 China has placed export licensing requirements on several critical minerals and related products, including gallium, germanium, graphite, antimony and some rare earths. The list changes, so check the latest announcements from the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and ask your supplier whether an export licence is needed.
Battery metals

Lithium, nickel and cobalt are growing fastest because of electric vehicles and energy storage. China refines a large share of the world's battery materials, much of it from ore mined abroad, and it dominates cell manufacturing. See our guide to
China's green energy sector
for the downstream side.
Environment, safety and governance
What are the main environmental challenges?

The main problems are the treatment of tailings and waste, acid drainage, and dust. The sector is also working to reduce emission intensity through cleaner energy and more efficient consumption. Stricter enforcement can close non-compliant mines and smelters quickly, which tightens supply.
How are safety and compliance handled?

Regulators carry out periodic inspections and close high-risk mines, raise safety standards for deep mines, and push for better disclosure and governance. After serious accidents, whole regions can halt production for checks, so a single incident can affect supply of a mineral for weeks. For you, this is a good reason to keep a second approved supplier for any critical metal input.
Which rules and frameworks apply?

The direction is stricter environmental regulation, ESG disclosure standards for listed companies, and state support for research into clean mining and urban recycling. If you are choosing suppliers partly on environmental grounds, our guide to
choosing environmentally friendly suppliers
sets out what to ask.
How are local communities managed?
The expected approach is early consultation, fair compensation, training and alternative employment programmes, and regular, transparent public monitoring of environmental impact.
Which indicators measure performance?
Accident rate per 1,000 workers
Emission intensity, measured in tonnes of CO2 per tonne of ore
Percentage of waste that is treated
Metal recovery rate in processing
If you invest in or partner with a mining or processing company, ask for these four figures for the past three years. A company that cannot produce them is a governance risk.
How do market swings affect you, and how can you protect yourself?

The sector is highly sensitive to commodity prices. China uses strategic stockpiling and futures hedging to manage the risk, particularly because it depends on imported iron ore and copper. Chinese futures markets are active: iron ore on the Dalian Commodity Exchange, copper and aluminium on the Shanghai Futures Exchange, and lithium carbonate on the Guangzhou Futures Exchange. Chinese suppliers watch these prices daily and often quote with short validity periods.

As a buyer, you cannot control these swings, but you can reduce their effect on your margin. Remember too that Chinese exporters usually quote metal-heavy goods in USD while their costs are in CNY, so a large exchange-rate move can also prompt a price revision.
Ask suppliers to break down quotations into metal content and processing cost, so you can see what a price change really affects.

Agree a price-adjustment clause linked to a public index, such as the Shanghai Futures Exchange or London Metal Exchange price, with a threshold (for example a move of more than 5%) before prices change.
Fix quotation validity in writing, typically 7 to 15 days for metal-heavy products, and pay the deposit within that window.
Split large orders into staged deliveries so you do not buy your whole annual volume at one price.
For large, regular volumes, talk to your bank about hedging, and get professional advice before using futures yourself.
Check export licence status for any critical mineral product before you pay, and build extra lead time into the contract if a licence is required.
Technology and where the sector is heading
Innovation stands out in automated smart mines, Internet of Things sensors, autonomous haul vehicles and digital twins used for predictive maintenance and schedule optimisation. Our article on
how China leads in robots and AI
covers the same trend in factories.

Over the next 3 to 5 years, expect deeper digitisation of mines, more low-carbon projects, expansion in recycling, and more international activity by Chinese companies along electric vehicle battery supply chains. The energy transition drives rising demand for copper, lithium and nickel from electric vehicles and renewable energy, with a gradual decline in coal's role.
Strategic trends: consolidation, local value and recycling

Three trends shape the sector. First, small operators are being merged into larger groups, which improves safety and control but reduces the number of independent sellers. Second, China is adding more value at home, especially in rare earths and batteries, by processing and manufacturing rather than exporting raw material. Third, Chinese companies invest in mines abroad to secure supply.
What is the status of urban mining and recycling?

Urban mining means recovering metals from electronic waste and industrial residues. Initiatives are growing, with government support to expand capacity and to count recycling towards emission reduction targets. For battery recycling, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) publishes a list of companies that meet its industry standards; check whether a potential partner is on it.
What opportunities exist for international partners?

Demand is strongest for low-emission equipment, clean processing technologies, safety solutions, recycling partnerships and hedging services. For Gulf companies the opportunity also runs the other way: Saudi Arabia's push to develop mining under Vision 2030, and wider Gulf investment in metals and processing, create demand for Chinese mining machinery, processing equipment and technical services.

Chinese mining machinery, such as excavators, crushers, conveyors and flotation equipment, is widely used in Africa, Central Asia and the Middle East. When you buy, compare the total cost over the life of the machine rather than the purchase price alone: power or fuel consumption, wear parts, service visits and resale value. Ask for references from customers in similar climates, because heat and dust in the Gulf shorten the life of seals, filters and electronics.
Before you buy metal products or mining equipment, work through this checklist:
Mill test certificate (for example EN 10204 type 3.1) showing grade and chemical composition
Independent laboratory test for grade, purity or coating thickness on a sample from your batch
Correct HS code and whether the item needs an export licence from China
Certificate of origin and any conformity certificate your country requires
Price-adjustment clause and quotation validity written into the contract
Pre-shipment inspection of quantity, markings and packing before the balance is paid
For equipment: spare parts availability, local service support and operator training
Common mistakes importers make
Accepting a quotation without checking how much of the price is metal content
Paying a deposit after the quotation has expired and then facing a price increase
Assuming every mineral product can be exported freely, without checking licence rules
Relying on the supplier's own test report instead of an independent one
Buying a full year's volume at one price during a market peak
Choosing a recycling or processing partner without checking its environmental compliance
What to do this week

List the metal-heavy products you buy from China and the metal each one depends on. For your largest order, ask the supplier for a cost breakdown, add a price-adjustment clause and confirm whether any export licence applies. Then book an independent test or inspection for the next shipment. HiGreenPanda can find and vet suppliers on the ground through our
product sourcing
service.

keyTakeaways: Iron ore, copper and lithium prices drive the cost of Chinese steel, cable and batteries, so watch the related futures prices.
Ask suppliers to split quotations into metal content and processing cost before agreeing a price.
Add a price-adjustment clause linked to a public index and fix quotation validity in writing.
Check whether any critical mineral product you buy needs a Chinese export licence before paying.
Use an independent laboratory test or inspection rather than the supplier's own report.

faqs.question: What minerals does China mine the most?
faqs.answer: Coal is the largest by volume and still supplies more than half of China's primary energy. China is also a major producer of rare earths, aluminium and steel, and it is growing in battery materials such as lithium. It imports most of its iron ore and a large share of its copper concentrate.

faqs.question: Does China control the rare earth market?
faqs.answer: China leads the world in rare earth mining and holds an even larger share of processing. Since 2023 it has added export licensing requirements for several critical minerals and some rare earths. Check the latest MOFCOM announcements and ask your supplier whether a licence is needed.

faqs.question: Why do Chinese steel and copper prices change so quickly?
faqs.answer: The sector is highly sensitive to commodity prices, and China depends on imported iron ore and copper. Suppliers track futures prices on the Dalian and Shanghai exchanges daily. That is why quotations for metal-heavy products often have validity periods of only 7 to 15 days.

faqs.question: What is urban mining in China?
faqs.answer: Urban mining is the recovery of metals from electronic waste and industrial residues. It is growing with government support and counts towards China's emission reduction targets. For battery recycling, check whether a partner is on MIIT's list of companies meeting its industry standards.

faqs.question: What opportunities are there for foreign companies in China's mining sector?
faqs.answer: The strongest openings are in low-emission equipment, clean processing technology, safety solutions, recycling partnerships and hedging services. Gulf companies developing their own mining and metals projects can also source Chinese machinery, processing equipment and technical services.

ar.seoDescription: تشهد الصين انفتاحاً متزايداً في قطاع الرعاية الصحية أمام الاستثمار الأجنبي، مما يخلق فرصاً استثمارية جديدة للشركات العالمية. هذا الانفتاح مدفوع بالحاجة…

children.text: الانفتاح الجديد في قطاع الرعاية الصحية الصيني

تشهد الصين انفتاحاً متزايداً في قطاع الرعاية الصحية أمام الاستثمار الأجنبي، مما يخلق فرصاً استثمارية جديدة للشركات العالمية. هذا الانفتاح مدفوع بالحاجة المتزايدة لخدمات الرعاية الصحية المتقدمة والرغبة في جذب الخبرات والتقنيات الدولية.
الإصلاحات القانونية الحديثة:
في نوفمبر 2024، أعلنت اللجنة الصحية الوطنية خطة عمل تفصيلية لإنشاء مستشفيات مملوكة بالكامل للأجانب في 9 مدن رئيسية، بما في ذلك:
بكين وتيانجين وشنغهاي
نانجينغ وسوتشو وفوتشو
غوانغتشو وشنتشن ومنطقة هايتشو بأكملها
الفرص الاستثمارية الرئيسية:
الرعاية الصحية عبر الإنترنت
نمو هائل في منصات التطبيب عن بعد والخدمات الصحية الرقمية، مع تزايد الطلب على الحلول التكنولوجية الصحية.
الأجهزة الطبية
سوق متنامٍ للأجهزة الطبية المتقدمة، خاصة مع شيخوخة السكان وارتفاع مستويات المعيشة.
الذكاء الاصطناعي في الرعاية الصحية
استثمارات ضخمة في تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي للتشخيص والعلاج ومراقبة المرضى.
الخدمات المتخصصة
طلب متزايد على الخدمات الطبية المتخصصة والرعاية المتقدمة، خاصة في المدن الكبرى.
التحديات والمتطلبات:
الامتثال التنظيمي
ضرورة الالتزام باللوائح الصحية الصارمة والحصول على التراخيص المطلوبة.
الشراكات المحلية
أهمية بناء علاقات قوية مع الشركاء المحليين والمؤسسات الطبية الصينية.
فهم السوق المحلي
الحاجة لفهم عميق لاحتياجات المرضى الصينيين والممارسات الطبية المحلية.
الاستثمار في التدريب
تطوير قدرات الكوادر المحلية وتدريبها على التقنيات والممارسات الدولية.
السياسات المشجعة:
إدراج قطاع الرعاية الصحية في كتالوج الصناعات المشجعة للاستثمار الأجنبي
حوافز ضريبية للشركات العاملة في مناطق التنمية المعينة
تسهيلات في إجراءات التسجيل والترخيص
التوقعات المستقبلية:
من المتوقع أن يستمر نمو سوق الرعاية الصحية الصيني بمعدلات مرتفعة، مدفوعاً بـ:
الشيخوخة السكانية
زيادة الوعي الصحي
النمو الاقتصادي وارتفاع الدخول
التطور التكنولوجي السريع

en.title: China's Healthcare Industry: Opportunities for Foreign Companies
en.excerpt: China now allows fully foreign-owned hospitals in 9 locations and is opening telemedicine, medical devices and AI health to outside capital. Here is where the openings are, what licences they need and how to test the market first.
en.seoDescription: China's healthcare industry is opening to foreign firms: the 9 pilot locations for foreign hospitals, the 4 growth areas, the licences and how to start.

children.text: You may have heard that China now lets foreign companies own hospitals outright, and wondered whether that opening reaches a trader or investor from the Gulf. China's healthcare industry is opening to foreign investment faster than at any point in the last 20 years, but every door comes with a licence, a local partner question and a long approval clock. By the end of this guide you will know which segments are open, what the 2024 reforms changed, what the regulator expects of you, and how to test the market before you commit capital.
Why China is opening healthcare to foreign companies

China needs more advanced healthcare than its public system can deliver. Its population is ageing, incomes in the large cities have risen, and patients who can pay increasingly want private, specialist care. Beijing's answer has been to invite foreign capital, foreign expertise and foreign technology into a sector that was, until recently, largely closed to them.

For you, that shift creates two kinds of opportunity. The first is investing in China itself: clinics, hospitals, digital health platforms or joint research. The second, which suits most Gulf importers, is trade: buying Chinese medical devices, consumables and health technology that are now built to higher standards because the domestic market demands it. The second route needs far less capital and teaches you the sector before you consider the first.
Policies that support the opening
Beijing has backed the opening with concrete measures:
Healthcare is included in the Catalogue of Industries for Encouraging Foreign Investment, which can bring lower tariffs on imported equipment for an approved project
Tax incentives are available for companies operating in designated development zones; the level depends on the zone and the activity, so ask the zone authority for its current terms in writing
Registration and licensing procedures have been simplified, with some cities and Hainan offering faster approval for foreign-invested medical projects
Incentives vary by city and change often. Treat any figure you hear at a conference as a starting point and confirm it with the local commerce bureau before you build it into a business plan.
What changed in 2024: fully foreign-owned hospitals

In November 2024, the National Health Commission announced a detailed action plan for establishing fully foreign-owned hospitals in 9 major locations. Before this, foreign investors could generally only hold a stake in a hospital through a joint venture with a Chinese partner. The pilot locations are:
Beijing, Tianjin and Shanghai
Nanjing, Suzhou and Fuzhou
Guangzhou, Shenzhen and the whole of Hainan, including Haikou

The pilot has limits. It is aimed at new hospitals rather than buying existing public ones, and traditional Chinese medicine hospitals have been treated separately. Check the current text of the notice and the provincial implementing rules before you plan anything, because each city publishes its own procedures, and approval still runs through the local health commission, which sets requirements for floor space, bed numbers and medical staff.
What this means in practice

A foreign-owned hospital is a multi-year, multi-million-dollar project. For most readers the reform matters less as a direct opportunity and more as a signal: China wants international healthcare providers in its biggest cities, and the suppliers, equipment makers and service firms around them will grow with that demand.
Four areas where foreign companies are finding opportunities
Online healthcare and telemedicine

Telemedicine platforms and digital health services have grown massively, and demand for health technology solutions keeps rising. Patients book appointments, consult doctors and buy prescription refills through apps. Foreign participation here is shaped by data rules: health data collected in China generally has to be stored in China, and sending it abroad requires a security assessment or another approved route. Budget for local hosting and legal review from the start.
Medical devices

The market for advanced medical devices is growing, pushed by an ageing population and rising living standards. Chinese manufacturers now make everything from disposable syringes to imaging systems. For a Gulf importer this is the most accessible segment: you can source Chinese-made devices for your home market without setting up anything in China. The rules are detailed in our guide to
China's medical devices and health technology industry
AI in healthcare

China is investing heavily in artificial intelligence for diagnosis, treatment and patient monitoring: image reading for radiology, triage chatbots, remote monitoring of chronic patients. The same push is transforming Chinese factories, as covered in
how China leads the smart manufacturing revolution
. AI-based diagnostic software counts as a medical device in China and in most Gulf states, so it needs registration like any other device.
Specialised services

Demand for specialist medical services and advanced care is rising, especially in the major cities: rehabilitation, elderly care, dentistry, fertility, cosmetic medicine and international-standard clinics for expatriates and wealthier residents. These are service businesses, so they depend on licensed staff and a strong local reputation more than on capital.
What the regulator and the market expect from you
The opening is real, but the sector remains one of the most tightly regulated in China. Four requirements come up in every project.
Regulatory compliance and licences

You must comply with strict health regulations and obtain every required licence. A medical institution needs a practice licence from the health commission. Medical devices sold in China are regulated by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) in three risk classes: Class I devices are filed, Class II and III devices need registration, which commonly takes 1 to 3 years for higher-risk products. Medicines follow a separate registration route, explained in our article on
China's pharmaceutical industry
Local partnerships

Strong relationships with local partners and Chinese medical institutions matter even where full foreign ownership is now allowed. Hospitals refer patients, universities supply doctors, and distributors control access to public hospital tenders. A partner who already holds the relevant licences can save you a year.
Understanding the local market

You need a deep understanding of Chinese patients' needs and local medical practice. Chinese patients expect fast service, digital booking and payment through Alipay or WeChat Pay, and many combine Western and traditional Chinese medicine. A model copied directly from Riyadh or Dubai will not fit.
Investment in training

Plan to develop local staff and train them on international technologies and practices. Equipment is only as good as the people using it, and regulators look at staff qualifications when they inspect.
How to enter China's healthcare industry step by step
Whether you are a Gulf distributor or an investor, the safest path moves from low-capital steps to high-capital ones:
Choose one segment and one product line. A distributor of dental consumables and an investor in a rehabilitation clinic face completely different rules.

Check the rules in both markets. In China, confirm whether your activity is open to foreign capital and which licence it needs. At home, confirm the device or product registration route with your regulator, for example the SFDA in Saudi Arabia or the federal health regulator in the UAE.
Start with trade. Source a small range of Chinese devices or health products for your home market. This builds supplier relationships and teaches you the standards without a Chinese entity.

Verify suppliers properly. Ask for the NMPA production licence (for Class II and III devices), the ISO 13485 certificate and any CE or FDA documents, and have the factory audited before the first order.
Visit China and the major trade fairs to meet hospitals, distributors and manufacturers, and shortlist 2 or 3 potential partners.
Only then decide on a local entity. A trading company, a joint venture or a wholly foreign-owned enterprise each carries different licensing and capital requirements.
When you reach the last step,
company formation in China
covers the entity choice, registered capital and the licences that follow.
Common mistakes foreign companies make
Treating the 2024 hospital reform as open to every city. It applies only to the 9 pilot locations, and each has its own procedure.
Assuming an EU CE certificate lets you sell a device in China. It does not; the device needs NMPA filing or registration.
Moving patient data out of China without checking the data export rules.
Choosing a local partner on personal introductions alone, without checking licences, court records and hospital relationships.
Importing medical devices to the Gulf without registering them first, then losing weeks while the shipment waits at the port.
Skipping pre-shipment inspection on sterile or electrical products, where one defective batch can end a distribution contract.
Quality problems cost more in healthcare than in almost any other sector, which is why independent
quality inspection
before shipment is worth building into every order.
The outlook for China's healthcare market
China's healthcare market is expected to keep growing at high rates, driven by four forces:
Population ageing, which raises demand for chronic care, rehabilitation and devices
Growing health awareness, which lifts spending on prevention, check-ups and supplements
Economic growth and rising incomes, which let more patients pay for private care
Rapid technological development, which keeps producing new devices, software and treatments

Competition from Chinese firms is intense, and prices for standard products are falling as local makers scale up. The lasting openings for foreign companies are in areas where they bring something local firms lack: clinical expertise, international brands, management systems or access to overseas markets, including the Gulf.
What to do this week

Write down the one segment you are most interested in and whether you want to trade or invest. Then check your home regulator's registration requirements for that product type, and ask 3 Chinese suppliers for their NMPA licence, ISO 13485 certificate and export history. If you want to talk through the entry route before you spend money,
book a consultation
and bring your product list.

keyTakeaways: Fully foreign-owned hospitals are allowed only in 9 pilot locations, from Beijing and Shanghai to Shenzhen and Hainan; check each city's rules.
For most Gulf businesses, sourcing Chinese medical devices is the lowest-capital way into China's healthcare industry.
Medical devices in China fall into three NMPA classes; a CE mark alone does not allow sale inside China.
Ask every device supplier for its NMPA production licence, ISO 13485 certificate and export records before the first order.
Confirm tax incentives and zone benefits in writing with the local authority before building them into your plan.

faqs.question: Can foreign companies own hospitals in China?
faqs.answer: Yes, under a pilot announced in 2024. Fully foreign-owned hospitals can be set up in Beijing, Tianjin, Shanghai, Nanjing, Suzhou, Fuzhou, Guangzhou, Shenzhen and the whole of Hainan. Elsewhere, foreign investors generally still need a joint venture with a Chinese partner.

faqs.question: Which parts of China's healthcare industry are growing fastest?
faqs.answer: Online healthcare and telemedicine, medical devices, AI for diagnosis and monitoring, and specialised private services such as rehabilitation and elderly care. Growth is driven by an ageing population, rising incomes, health awareness and new technology.

faqs.question: Do I need a company in China to import Chinese medical devices?
faqs.answer: No. You can buy directly from Chinese manufacturers as a foreign importer. You do need to register the devices with your own country's regulator, such as the SFDA in Saudi Arabia, and verify the supplier's NMPA licence and ISO 13485 certificate.

faqs.question: What licences do foreign healthcare companies need in China?
faqs.answer: It depends on the activity. A clinic or hospital needs a medical institution practice licence from the local health commission. Medical devices need NMPA filing (Class I) or registration (Class II and III), and medicines need drug registration.

faqs.question: Are there tax incentives for foreign healthcare investment in China?
faqs.answer: Healthcare is in the encouraged foreign investment catalogue, and designated development zones offer tax incentives. The terms vary by zone and activity, so confirm them in writing with the local authority before you commit.
